name: AI Semantic Expansion
description: Enriches Search API indexes with AI-generated semantic synonyms and search intents, enabling database-agnostic semantic search without a vector store.
project_description:
AI Semantic Expansion enriches Drupal Search API indexes with AI-generated synonyms and likely search-intent phrases so semantically related content ranks on ordinary keyword backends (Database, Solr, Elasticsearch) with no vector database or embeddings infrastructure.

The module ships one Search API processor (AiIntentExpander, id ai_intent_expander) that exposes a virtual index property, ai_semantic_synonyms, which you map as a Fulltext field and boost. Crucially, that processor makes NO live AI calls at index time: it only reads pre-generated text from a local cache table {ai_semantic_cache}. Generation is asynchronous. On node insert/update the module's hooks queue the node (only when some index has the processor enabled); the ai_semantic_expansion_queue QueueWorker runs on cron, builds source text from the configured fields (title/body/summary/tags, HTML stripped, length-limited), and calls the configured LLM through the drupal/ai provider abstraction to produce a comma-separated synonym/intent list. Results are cached and re-generated only when an MD5 content hash of the source text changes, so unchanged nodes never re-hit the API.

All AI text generation and cache management lives in AiSemanticExpansionService, which resolves the provider/model from config, sends a ChatInput with a configurable system prompt, and returns an empty string on any provider failure so indexing is never blocked. A Drush command, ai-expand:batch (alias aieb), pre-warms the cache for existing content by exporting source-text payloads to a private:// JSONL file then processing each line, keeping memory flat at tens of thousands of nodes. Changing the LLM prompt in the processor form clears the cache and re-queues all nodes; a "Flush AI cache now" button truncates the cache on demand. Requires Drupal 10.4+/11, drupal/ai with at least one chat provider, drupal/search_api, and a configured private files directory for the batch export.
